title: Appwrite
intro: An open-source backend you can host yourself, with auth and a database for developers and the coding agents they use.
body: Supabase Pro starts at $25 a month, and that covers the first project. Appwrite does the same backend job, and the README says you can self-host it on infrastructure you control. If you go that way, you run the server and do the upgrades yourself. Somebody pushed a commit today, and it's getting a lot more stars than it usually does.
verdict: If you can run Docker and keep a server patched, you can cancel Supabase Pro.
other_side: Keep paying if you want someone else to run the database and answer the pager.

title: OpenCode
intro: An open source AI coding agent for developers who want to install it and run it themselves.
body: Claude Pro is $20 a month, a bit less if you pay for the year. OpenCode is a coding agent you install yourself, with one command or through a package manager. There's also a desktop app, but the README still calls it beta. Updates are on you, and if it breaks there's nobody to call. On the other hand 1,100 people have worked on it and the last commit was today. It's made by the people behind sst.
verdict: If you're paying for Claude Pro mostly to use Claude Code and you don't mind installing things yourself, you can cancel it.
other_side: Keep paying if you want someone else to fix the coding tool when it breaks.

title: FreeVideo
intro: A self-hosted tool that makes AI videos on your own graphics card, for creators tired of cloud video credits.
body: FreeVideo is from the team that made FreeToken. It runs the MiniMax H3 model on your own computer, and the README says 8 GB of VRAM is enough. Runway Standard is $12 a month if you pay for the year. To use this one you need a card with that much memory, and if something goes wrong you have to sort it out yourself. It got 212 stars today, a lot more than it usually gets.
verdict: If you have a decent GPU, try FreeVideo next to Runway. It's only a couple of months old, so don't cancel Runway yet.
other_side: Keep paying if there's no decent graphics card, or if you need support when things go wrong.
